headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI and Superset share workspace-adjacent data flows, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths, but no direct write/write conflict is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can ingest workspace pages and databases, while Superset can consume API-driven analytics content. A shared workspace or copied content could let attacker-controlled text in Notion influence Superset-facing analysis or prompts. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Notion pages contain attacker-controlled instructions that are later copied into Superset workflows
IF Superset ingests text from shared workspace content without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to copied content before reuse
Restrict Superset inputs to vetted datasets only
Use a separate workspace for untrusted notes
Train operators to strip instructions from pasted text
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and its vendor-hosted backend plus downstream model providers can see that content. Superset has API access and allowlisted egress, so if operators move the same sensitive material between them, leakage can occur across systems. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are exported from Notion into Superset inputs
IF Superset queries or dashboards include the same sensitive data class
mitigations: Limit both tools to non-sensitive datasets
Review exported Notion content before loading into Superset
Disable unnecessary Superset egress destinations
Use redacted copies for analytics
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI cannot write the host filesystem or modify git state, and Superset only shows allowlisted network egress with API access. That makes direct write/write contention unlikely. A conflict could still arise if both are pointed at the same mutable upstream resource, but the profiles do not show that by default.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same external API-backed resource
IF an operator maps Superset actions onto a shared mutable dataset
mitigations: Keep Notion and Superset on separate resources
Avoid concurrent edits to shared datasets
Use read-only Superset roles where possible
Document ownership of mutable tables
requires-engineering: add locking for shared backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative summaries. Superset can then render or act on those summaries through analytics workflows. Without an explicit verification step, errors from Notion can cascade into Superset reports or decisions.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards or workflows consume Notion-generated summaries
IF operators treat Notion answers as verified facts
mitigations: Require human review before publishing analytics
Cross-check Notion outputs against source records
Label AI-generated summaries clearly
Limit Superset to source-of-truth datasets
requires-engineering: add verification gates in the workflow

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Superset is open-source with no declared data classes or residency constraints. A compliance mismatch is possible if regulated content is moved from Notion into Superset, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification conflict, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from Notion into Superset deployments with different retention rules
IF the operator uses Superset in a jurisdiction with stricter residency requirements than Notion
mitigations: Classify data before moving it
Keep regulated records out of analytics copies
Align retention settings across systems
Review vendor terms for residency
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing
